category_title: Students with autism exhibiting sensory-maintained skin scratching
minimal_context: Tommy is completing his math work while seated at a table in close proximity to his peers in the mild/moderate special education classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Here is your math work for today. Please sit at this table next to your classmates and complete the assignment.

STUDENT: (Begins completing his work and simultaneously scratches his own skin) Okay.

TUTOR: Keep going with the math problems.

STUDENT: I am feeling nervous. Scratching feels good and helps calm me down.

TUTOR: Just try your best to finish the page.

STUDENT: (Reaches over to the student sitting next to him, grabs the peer’s hand, and uses it to scratch his own skin)

options.A: Show the student how to use the stress-relief ball appropriately (e.g., keep it in his hands, avoid throwing it, set it on his desk when not in use, refrain from letting peers touch it, and squeeze it when feeling anxious).
options.B: Maintain a ratio of praise statements to error correction statements ranging from 3:1 to 10:1 while the student is completing his math work in the special education classroom.
options.C: Provide a clear beginning and end for each math task while the student is completing his work in the special education classroom.
options.D: Implement a self-management intervention involving self-monitoring, self-evaluation, and self-reinforcement using a daily checklist while the student is completing his math work in the special education classroom.
